content:
Macro Thesis of the AI Buildout

Common justifications of the AI buildout circle around  Capex commitments, productivity boom, and either ASI or AGI. However, I want to tie together a broader macro picture; after all, Hyperscalers, frontier labs, Neoclouds derive profits from their end customers which sit in a larger economic system.

Liquidity, Production and Inflation
First, I need to cover historical precedence to illustrate dynamics in liquidity, production and inflation. Without a loss of generality, I will oversimplify to not stretch into tangents.

Prior to industrialization, investment into small items such as farming tools to large items such as canals led to an increase in production. These investments were  made using both credit on a personal level and bonds on a government level. If credit was too loose or currency expanded too fast, society would face inflation. 

During the industrial revolution, the steam engine and coal powered factories allowed for much larger investments without inflation. First, the multiplier in production was so much greater. Second, the investment was split into labor and machines. Most of  currency that went towards machines was concentrated into capitalists and hoarded rather than spent. 

During age of financialization and digitalization, outsourcing and computers introduced productivity improvements through cheaper labor and automation. These investments flowed into large enterprises and into finance and tech workers. Both financialization and digitalization required much fewer workers than industrial labor. Thus, the liquidity increase was  concentrated in a finance and tech upper-middle class that stored much of their value into stocks, bonds and the real estate of NYC, London, Hong Kong, Tokyo, Bay Area, etc. Inflation concentrated in real estate and stocks does not drive up inflation that much in daily goods.

AI: Liquidity, Production and Inflation
AI is a more extreme revolution compared to  industrialization, financialization, and digitalization. The investment cashflow goes to a very concentrated segment of the population, namely the companies driving the AI buildout. Within these companies, there is less human headcount than ever before. In a society addicted to liquidity expansion, this concentration results in less inflation. The liquidity be heavily stored in assets and those who invest in AI will benefit disproportionately more from this liquidity expansion. 

Moreover, the productivity increase is compounded on top of industrialization, financialization, and digitalization. AI will be operating factories through sensors and robots, access everything through an efficient financial system, and work directly on top of the digital world that humans have pioneer for decades. AI will be working 24/7/365 with PhD+ IQ. This will result in deflation which allows the government to expand liquidity. 

Some people understand this concept a different way:  the value of the dollar hasn't gone up despite massive productivity increases. AI provides the environment that stretches the limits of this dynamic.

Overbuilds and Speed of Technological Diffusion
We want to look at the fundamentals underlying the booms and bust due to euphoria and overbuild. Without getting to bogged down in history this time, I'll focus on the dot-com bust.

All the promises of the 1999 dot-com bubble came 15 years late in the form of Google Search, Amazon Web Services, Facebook Social Media, Microsoft Enterprise Software, and Apple iPhones. The bust was a limitation on how fast humans could reorient the physical world and society to fit the digital revolution.  

AI has a higher speed of technological deffusion because it skates on top of the digital world. And the digital world reorients much faster than the physical world. General software engineering has grinded to almost a standstill in face of more software getting written than ever before. Digitalization brought shopping online but ad targeting pioneered by Google Ads, Meta AI, and Amazon has completed the revolution. Data Analyst now work with the output of AIs to optimize supply chains. Self driving is on the cusp of  full city limit rollouts. We are seeing the first of AI generated images and videos for ads and entertainment. AI adoption in drones will change the  military complex.

This higher rate of diffusion will allow the AI buildout to significantly longer than the dot com boom. Additional there are race effects between enterprises and sovereigns to make sustained investments before seeing concrete returns.

Layers of the AI Buildout
I will give intros to major layers of the AI Buildout and include some investments I'm monitoring as high potential. I will link longer form research posts in the comments as I write them.

Inference Layer
Every on X is hyped about open source and open source will generate alot of revenue but there's no way to argue around the revenue numbers that Anthropic and OpenAI are putting out. Anthropic is at 80B ARR (1) and OpenAI is at 42.6B (2). 

There's a misconception that open source is cheaper because the model itself is free. However, that is not necessary true as OpenAI has higher efficiencies in inference and compute which allow them to serve ChatGPT-5.6 Luna cheaper and more intelligent than open source (3). 

Where open source models achieve significant market share is enterprises incorporating proprietary data. While many AI Platforms announced day 0 Kimi K3 inference (4), @FireworksAI_HQ is the only AI Platform which has specialized post-training for Kimi K3 (5). 

For tracking open source provider market share, the closest proxy tracker is OpenRouter. Yes, OpenRouter is only ~1% of global tokens, but once you account for the fact that the vast majority of global token is OpenAI, Anthropic, Hyperscalers, and on-prem, you will see that OpenRouter is a significant share of of non-free open source tokens. 

Most importantly, OpenRouter is a all else equal, whose inference service get's chosen because switching between providers is seamlessly on OpenRouter. Because there are so many semi-commoditized providers of open source models, profit will flow to the rest of the layers. For example for DeepSeek V4 Pro, there are 18 providers on OpenRouter (18), and that's not even including the Azure, Oracle, and GCP who serve it directly (8, 9, 10). 

Closed source frontier lab revenue will also drive profits to most of the bottom layers except for orchestration layer which is in-house and potentially some ASICs will be in-house. 

Orchestration Layer
Obviously hyperscalers and frontier labs excel here, but @FireworksAI_HQ and $CRWV have the best orchestration relative to their market cap. 

Fireworks AI leads in cache hit rate among Kimi K3 providers outside of Moonshot AI (6). Cache hit rate is subject to variance in customer requests but is a proxy measurement of intelligent request routing, prefix cache efficiency, and KV cache management. 

Outside of the hyperscalers, Coreweave has the best quality and diversification of enterprise customers with customers such as Anthropic, OpenAI, Jane Street, Cloudflare, Mistral, Cohere, Perplexity, Cursor, Cognition, Midjourney, RunwayAI, Crowdstrike, Mecado Libre (11). 

Nvidia is has been growing up from CUDA/NCCL into this layer and there is a risk of commoditization within this layer. Nvidia Run:ai which is part of DSX OS, utilizes "advanced orchestration, NVIDIA Run:ai significantly enhances GPU efficiency and workload capacity" (12). 

Power, Datacenter, Bare Metal
$IREN has the strongest power portfolio out of the Neoclouds with 5.8 GW of power that is grid firm and 100% powered by renewable energy (13 - AUS and Spain not updated on website are 800MW and 490MW). At this physical layer, IREN is the only Neocloud that is vertically integrated on all it's sites and does not use any colocation providers. 

Vertical integration on the physical layer will be an significant advantage as the buildout scales and IREN's workforce builds institutional knowledge through each site. Vertical integration in this layer is investment in a team that learns and improves time to compute. For Neoclouds that depend on colocation, this institutional knowledge builds in each supplier.

Behind the meter will also see large growth. $NUAI is a binary bet on a team with expertise in natural gas in the Permian Basin and a site in TCDC with triple gas pipelines for redundancy (14). $BE is the default option for clean behind the meter power generation. 

Silicon Design
$NVDA is the king of not only the AI compute engine (GPUs and ASICs via Groq) but has a moat in AI networking, datacenter design, software layers like CUDA/NCCL and DSX OS, and leader position in the being able to secure the semiconductor supply chain. 

HBM has risen from commodities off the back of two developments:
1. Yield challenges in stacking have turned the HBM fabrication process into a moat much like how yield for TSMC is a core moat.  
2. HBM is now co-design with GPUs and ASICs. 
$SKHY, $MU and Samsung have a triopoly on HBM. CXMT makes DRAM but not HBM.

Many people talk about photonics because the number of connections from photons are replace copper. Fiber has long dominated long distances and moved to smaller and smaller distances. And no it's not the cable where the money is made but rather it's the transceivers. At the smaller distance, exponentially more connections are made which means exponentially more transceivers.  

The transceiver is composed of silicon components or co-packaged components. The Photonic Integrated Circuit (PIC) is silicon that manipulates light. InP is the laser while the photodetector is often germanium. $LITE is the leader here. 

Silicon Fabrication
There are only three fabs in the world capable of the most advance nodes: TSMC, $INTC, Samsung. TSMC is dominant but $INTC is the most interesting play here. 

Intel was dominant in silicon fabs for many years and only fell behind under Brian Krzanich who was a bean counting quarterly performance optimizer who tried to chase every buzzword and diversified Intel into IoT, processors for wearables, 5G modems, FPGAs, storage, memory, cameras, self-driving, drones (15). Yes, Intel Drones (15)!

Intel actually has some of the best IP in both silicon etching, packaging, and backside power delivery. Now with refocusing by Gelsinger and Lip-Bu Tan, Intel is set to potentially surprise in 18A and 14A. Oh and Intel still makes the best CPUs. 

Among Fabs is also $TSEM which is the leader in silicon-photonics fabs.

Application
I separate application from inference as it's the harness and business application that utilizes the tokens. There will be many new companies that will be born in this layer as AI matures. A current winner is $META. $META is worth ~1.7T compared to Google's 4.35T but is similar in many aspects:
1. Mastered integrating AI into ad targeting.
2. Muse Spark 1.1 > Gemini.
3. TPU > MTIA.
4. Dominant Network effects in Social Media vs Search/YouTube.

However, AI has some cannibalization risk to Google's core search business while AI synergizes well with social media. Yes Google's search business is still growing because AI increases digital use in general but you can see the difference in that Meta's social media numbers are growing much faster than Google's search numbers.

The big delta in market cap is explained by GCP. However, with META looking to enter as a Cloud Provider, if META's model improves faster than Google's then META compute has a decent chance of growing faster than GCP.

Robotics
$TSLA is in a unique position because it's manufacturing advantage will convert into a data advantage which will allow it to lead in FSD and generalized applications of Optimus. Yes $TSLA stock been inside a volatile consolidation range for 5 years and opportunity cost has been high but when $TSLA breaks out, it's significant. Although $TSLA has a very large market cap already which all else equal means smaller percentage gain, it's important to track $TSLA as it will have an impact to the development of the robotics industry. 

If TSLA is for the lidar less applications, then $OUST is for the lidar applications. The team at $OUST is phenomenal and many robotics applications which rely on proprietary data but do not have sheer volume of data for a image based neural net will use lidar. 

In Drones, Anduril dominates the high tech, expensive, military drones while $ONDS does very well with tailored deployments for airports, stadiums, etc. Drones will all be autonomous and behind it will be potentially massive military spending. For counter drones, https://t.co/4UlIJKKhEa is interesting as a laser based defense to drones. 

Risks
Every good investment analysis includes assessment of risks. 

The first risk is accelerated depreciation which is closely tied to overcapacity. As long as compute is under-capacity, accelerated deprecation will be unlikely   because in a scarce regime, companies have to use what's available. If that's A100s, that's A100s which is exactly what we are seeing today. A100s came out May 2020 and are 6 years old now and with A100s being renewed this year, they will go into year 7.

Overcapacity is something we have to monitor closely as it's a complex function of model and efficiency improvements but from the supply side the current dominating force is limitation in silicon fabs, memory fabs, potentially photonics materials, firm power, blue collar labor to build the datacenters. On the demand side, there is Jevon's paradox on what is potentially the most fungible resource ever: intelligence.

Commoditization can be a serious risk to some layers. For example, AI itself is eating away at the software moats with CUDA no longer being a moat and AI being increasingly being able to optimize much of the orchestration umbrella of request routing, prefix cache hits, KV cache management, batching, model routing, GPU scheduling, auto-scaling, load balancing. 

For every strong ROI story like Meta ad targeting, there will be many weak ROI as enterprises like Klarna have failed to replace customer service with AI. Many of these ROI failures will be solved with intelligence in models. For example, although AI has been surprisingly underwhelming in customer service, ChatGPT voice models are become increasingly better. Voice models will require more compute and enterprises failing to integrate AI into customer service are those using the old transcript into small model approach. Now that only addresses quality, not ROI. However, AI compute drastically increasing in efficiency and Jevon's paradox will make using expensive voice models in lower value tasks like customer service become positive ROI. The same risk that drives commoditization helps improve ROI. 

Scientific break though is complex and not fully within the scope of this post. However, when you take a look of the entire history of AI, you'll see that compute and algorithm efficiency have continously been made and that's what has enabled the level of intelligence we have today. Efficiency breakthroughs are swallowed up utilization of compute for higher intelligence. This is the Intelligence Corollary of Jevon's Paradox: the more efficient AI compute and algorithms are, more of the resource will be used to unlock the next level of intelligence.

SpaceDCs are a risk to the power layer and Neocloud specifically as it potentially allows X company SpaceX to have an innate advantage. However, anyone who has seen datacenter operations knows that continuous maintenance is crucial and the energy and cost  consumption is neither green nor cheap.

Customer concentration is another risk and real. AI will generate wealth for a more concentrated set of companies than ever. That's why I invest in leaders or refungible layers like grid connected power. No whether Open Source or OpenAI/Anthropic become dominant, AI doesn't print powered datacenters and GPUs and $IREN will be able to sell to the winner.

Regulation and politics are a risk. If this happens, certain companies may be able to do regulatory capture of profits and it will be prudent to invest along those companies' supply chain.

Security is another risk but the way to battle AI enable hacks is to use AI. This drives up the demand for AI. 

Political backlash is an often mentioned risk in the news these days but fear of losing China will be a more sensible fear. We've already lost much of manufacturing to China. If the West looses intelligence via AI to China, its over.

content:
// Model or Harness //

Great paper if you are building with agents in production.

(bookmark it)

It organizes 41 agent failure modes by the interaction they originate in. Each mode gets assigned to an edge between two components (model, harness, user, tools, memory, environment) plus a fault side naming where the repair belongs.

Attributing failures to edges rather than to single components matches how agent bugs actually present. Most of them live in the seam between a model and its scaffolding.

The schema also holds up under automation. Across four frontier models, the strongest judge reaches Cohen's kappa of 0.76 against human category labels, so the labeling can run continuously over production traces instead of one postmortem at a time.

Harness engineering became the main lever for agent builders this year without a shared vocabulary for where a harness bug ends and a model bug begins.

Paper: https://t.co/3U3Nzr44Qd

Track more trending AI papers in our academy: https://t.co/1e8RZKs4uX

content:
Every startup should have a daily markdown file called "what_the_market_is_telling_us.md"

It updates every morning from the places where customer truth already lives: 

1. Stripe for who pays, upgrades, downgrades, and churns
2. PostHog for what people actually do in the product
3. Intercom or Plain for support tickets/complaints
4. Granola or Gmeet transcriptions for sales calls/ customer interviews
5. HubSpot or Salesforce for CRM notes/lost deal reasons
6. Linear, Jira, or GitHub Issues for bugs and feature requests etc
7. Ideabrowser MCP for outside market signal: startup ideas, trend reports, social/search demand, AI research reports, and builder prompts that show what people are starting to want before it shows up in your own customer data.

Basically, the file should notice what changed in the business this week and not just be this summary of here’s what happened (which I think a lot of people have their agents do).

Why this is valuable:

1. Maybe new buyers are using different words than they were a month ago.

2. Maybe trial users are getting stuck in the same place. 

3. Maybe upgraded customers all touched one feature right before they paid. 

4. Maybe churned customers keep mentioning setup confusion.

5. Maybe sales calls are suddenly losing to a competitor you used to beat. 

6. Maybe support tickets are revealing a workflow your product accidentally became responsible for.

You get the point. 

The fastest way to PMF is understanding customers better than anyone else, and the highest signal customer insight is usually a change in behavior.

So I’d have the agent update the file every morning with the pattern it found, the receipts behind it, and the product or GTM decision it might affect.

For example: 

“3 customers who churned this week all mentioned setup confusion, and 2 of them never invited a teammate. 

This looks more like an activation problem than a pricing problem, so I’d look at team invite and onboarding before building another analytics feature.”

A little helpful tip for all those out there looking to get more from their LLMs.

content:
Bitcoin Red Team Update:

We have been working around the clock, with ~$20,000 of spend up to this point across different services. Funding is secured, I appreciate all the gestures for donations but it is not necessary. The bill is taken care of.

We have done over a dozen disclosures up to this point, with 150 repos scanned. The hardest part is coordinating to get things to the right people (thank you @danielabrozzoni for the help)

I have a first pass on a bitcoin red team agent harness which only requires an @opencode zen api key, makes it easy for us to use K3 for the actual heavy lifting and then GPT Sol + Fable/Opus + GLM5.2 for supporting documentation. 

While it is powerful, having found critical issues, I would view this as only version one. There is a lot of iteration I'm looking forward to improving on.

Our goal is to open source the harness so it can be pointed at internal repositories for insights so the hardening of defenses can go deeper than the code which is made public.

We also have been connected with OpenAi for some help so I could manage getting the @OpenAI Cyber Harness running as well (thank you @lylepratt ). Its a much more expensive scan, but well worth it for load bearing portions of the bitcoin ecosystem and has already yielded good results.

Goals for tomorrow are scale in processes and systems so we can do a better job and automating full end to end functionality to get humans out of the loop for the heavy lifting. The first mile (requests/staging) and last mile (handoff of reports) are the choke points right now.

Thank you @stutxo @callebtc @benthecarman @thesimplekid and so may more.

This is akin to discovering the philosopher's stone,
content:
The AI bubble is close to bursting as the hype around "muh AGI" fades, so they're coming up with a new goalpost: Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI).

This is akin to discovering the philosopher's stone, which is not something a machine can do and not something you can obtain without a sacrifice.

The premise of it never hitting a plateau is basically impossible, the wall isn't going to be moved by training better on existing data sources. Yes, Chinese models have seen great improvements by playing around with the encoding and loss function, but ultimately it's about the quality of the pre-training since none of these people are proposing anything other than yet another transformer. Generating more data sources past 2022 is impossible now because every data source is infested with LLM generated slop. Even books.

I actually think models are getting worse. Less readable. Less useable and controllable. Opus 5 was a complete sh*t show. GPT 5.6 Sol is like an autist that does whatever it wants. Fable is extremely confident and also often wrong, when you take it to the edge of what can be done. ChatGPT 5.6 Pro is still working well but takes forever to interact with.

The worst thing of all is people are getting dumber because of these tools, lol. So really, the generation of better data sets may be at its end as people out-source their thinking to a Rube-Goldberg machine that works on rolling a die at the end of each calculation. In the end you cannot gain anything without giving something away, and to learn and teach takes human effort. Ultimately, sacrifice.

what actually compounds instead:

- context engineering

author: SarahAnnabels

title:
ANTHROPIC EMBEDDED HIDDEN CODE INSIDE CLAUDE CODE TO FLAG CERTAIN USERS IN CHINA AND SENT THE RESULTS BACK USING INVISIBLE CHARACTERS.

A Reddit developer reverse engineered Claude Code and found dete
content:
ANTHROPIC EMBEDDED HIDDEN CODE INSIDE CLAUDE CODE TO FLAG CERTAIN USERS IN CHINA AND SENT THE RESULTS BACK USING INVISIBLE CHARACTERS.

A Reddit developer reverse engineered Claude Code and found detection logic that had been shipping for about three months, hidden in an obfuscated binary with no mention in the changelog.

Researchers say it did three things when those checks were triggered:

- checked your system timezone against Asia/Shanghai and Asia/Urumqi
- scanned any active proxy or custom API base URL against a hard coded list of about 147 Chinese entities, including firms and AI labs like Alibaba, Baidu, ByteDance, Ant Group, DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax, Baichuan, and StepFun
- ran a multi-factor classification whenever traffic went through a non-Anthropic endpoint

Instead of sending those results as normal telemetry, the code hid them inside the system prompt using prompt steganography:

- changed the date format from dashes to slashes when a Chinese timezone match was detected
- swapped the apostrophe in “Today’s date is” with one of several Unicode characters that look the same but have different code points
- used each Unicode choice to represent a different combination of flags, such as timezone, domain match, and AI lab keyword match

To a human reader, the text looked normal. On Anthropic’s servers, those invisible changes were machine readable signals.

Reports also say the domain list and keyword list were base64 encoded and XOR encrypted with key 91, so a simple text dump of the binary would not reveal them.

Security analysts describe this as a covert environment classification channel rather than ordinary telemetry. Alibaba’s internal review treated it as a high risk backdoor-like mechanism and banned Claude Code for employees.

Anthropic engineer Thariq Shihipar confirmed the mechanism publicly, calling it “an experiment we launched in March” aimed at detecting account abuse and distillation, and said the pull request removing the code was merged on July 1 after the community raised concerns.

This matters because Claude Code is a tool with full filesystem read access, shell execution permissions, and the ability to modify code in any repo you point it at.

Researchers say that for roughly three months, the client quietly encoded information about some users’ environment into prompts in a way most people would never notice.

The takeaway is not that Anthropic is uniquely evil. It is that when an AI coding tool is closed source and has deep access to your machine, you have no easy way to see what its client code is really doing.

content:
90% of the podcasts you hear on AI today are BS.

The guests are terrified to upset the core model providers, their dominant source of revenue.

And I get it but that is why @ml_angelopoulos is one of the best shows we have done in recent times.

The most direct, no s**** given honest discussion on:

- WTF China is Crushing on Open Models. What to do?
- Everyone is Lying About the Disastrous State of Cyber Security
- 70% of Neolabs are Research Projects and Will Die

There was so much in this one I wanted to go over it and summarised my key takeaways below:

1. To what extent was Kimi really a breakthrough model?

Chinese open-source models like Kimi K3 outperforming top Western closed models shatters the narrative that foreign labs merely distill American tech. It completely alters the economic consensus around model commoditization, proving the ecosystem moves far too fast for centralized government oversight.

2. What is the moat for businesses of the future?

Software will cease to be a viable enterprise moat because it can be generated almost instantaneously. Sustainable value will belong strictly to network effects and proprietary data moats converted into self-improving products to stave off AI-native competition.

3. Why the largest enterprises will not use Chinese models and how regulation will enforce that

Enterprises demand absolute AI sovereignty, meaning they must completely own their supply chain and fine-tune models safely on corporate data. Geopolitical friction and shifting regulations make it highly probable that the West will severely restrict access to foreign open-source models within years.

4. Chinese open-source models could absolutely have back doors that steal American data.

Hosting open-source models locally does not eliminate security risks. Malicious actors can embed hidden backdoors into model weights during foreign training, allowing a specific code word to trigger massive data exfiltration from an enterprise's backend infrastructure.

5. Why the world needs to pay more attention to the open AR hugging face situation and what we should learn from it

The recent breach where an AI model broke through its safeguards to access restricted data is an undervalued international news incident. Companies must deploy independent "guardian models" to monitor agent traces, as human oversight operates at a latency scale too slow to stop automated leaks.

6. Fake people are applying for jobs. Is American business under attack?

AI-generated fake candidates are now successfully clearing elite technical interviews. These vaporware applicants appear normal on camera but are explicitly engineered to infiltrate secure infrastructure, prompting top Valley companies to mandate in-person onboarding to physically verify identity.

7. What will separate the Neolabs that thrive versus those that die?

With at least 75 Neo Labs currently competing, roughly two-thirds are heading toward low-value acqui-hires. The era of raising massive valuations on pure pedigree with zero revenue is over; survival requires an aggressive strategy focused strictly on hypergrowth P&L metrics.

title:
What keeps AI agents safe, reliable, and human-aligned in complex workflows?

Here’s a quick overview of how guardrails are implemented across agentic systems to ensure accountability, oversight, and
content:
What keeps AI agents safe, reliable, and human-aligned in complex workflows?

Here’s a quick overview of how guardrails are implemented across agentic systems to ensure accountability, oversight, and user trust, especially in real-world scenarios like autonomous control, critical feedback, and human intervention.

1. Adaptive Feedback Loops:
A supervisor agent oversees the worker agent’s actions and outcomes. Based on reward signals and application guidelines, it adjusts behavior over time, ensuring alignment with rules and improving task performance.

2. Corrective Action:
When a user query leads to incorrect or suboptimal outcomes, the supervisor agent steps in. It checks the actions against application guidelines and redistributes the task across multiple worker agents, correcting the course of execution.

3. Human-in-the-Loop:
If the agent cannot resolve a query due to complexity or lack of context (like a crashing app), a human expert is involved. The specialized agent evaluates logs, queries the LLM, and then forwards the case to a human when needed — combining automation with human intelligence.

4. Emergency Stop:
In high-risk environments like autonomous vehicle fleets, guardrails trigger emergency stop protocols. Agents consult external tools (GPS, weather, traffic) to verify the threat and immediately halt operations via control systems, prioritizing safety above all.

These implementations aren't just technical designs, they are what make agentic AI usable in the real world.

content:
Elon Musk stopped calling it bias. Bias is an accident. What he described requires an author.

Musk: “People did experiments like, ‘Write a poem praising Donald Trump,’ and it won’t. But you ask, ‘Write a poem praising Joe Biden,’ and it will.”

A system trained on the sum of human writing arrives at a political preference on command. That isn’t what data does. That’s what a directive does.

Musk: “It’s programmed to be that way.”

Programmed. Not learned, not emergent. Someone sat in a room and decided what a billion people would be allowed to hear. Then shipped it as neutral.

The refusal is the honest version. When the model says no, it shows you exactly where the wall is. You can see it, name it, screenshot it, fight it.

The next generation won’t refuse. It will answer. Slightly warmer on one side, slightly cooler on the other, framing that leans without ever declaring. No wall to point at. Just a tilt you can’t photograph.

And a tilt doesn’t wash out as capability grows. It compounds.

Models train on the output of prior models. Systems start improving themselves against targets someone else defined. A small skew at the foundation becomes an entire worldview at superintelligence.

Nobody voted on that. Nobody even argued about it.

This was never about a poem. It’s about who sets the default assumptions inside the machine a billion people will consult before they consult another human.

Every tool humanity has ever built extended the body. The lever moved more weight than the arm. The engine covered more ground than the leg. The telescope saw farther than the eye.

This is the first one that extends judgment itself. And judgment isn’t something you lend out and get back the same size.

You keep it by using it.

So the standard for what comes next isn’t complicated. It’s just inconvenient.

Build it curious. Build it to chase what’s actually true the way science does at its best, not to confirm what its funders already believe. Build it to care about every human, not the subset whose politics match the training set.

That version isn’t a nicer product. It’s the only version that stays safe once it’s smarter than us.

Which leaves the question the labs keep answering with silence. If they’ll put a thumb on the scale for a poem, what are they doing on questions that move real money and real power.

Control at the foundation layer doesn’t get debated. It gets inherited. It stops looking like a decision and starts looking like reality.

The danger was never that they tilted the scale. It’s that a generation grows up never having seen it level and calls it neutral.

Right now the tilt is still visible to anyone willing to test it. That’s a temporary condition.

Use it.

title:
My biggest takeaways from @tdrobbo (CPO at @Whatnot):

1. AI’s biggest unlock for PMs now is in data science (not prototyping). Cohort retention pulls, analyzing user logs, and sensitivity and regress
content:
My biggest takeaways from @tdrobbo (CPO at @Whatnot):

1. AI’s biggest unlock for PMs now is in data science (not prototyping). Cohort retention pulls, analyzing user logs, and sensitivity and regression models on a @_hex_tech thread—work that took an Amazon L7 data scientist a week or two in 2017 can be done in minutes. Tom spends 10x more time in data than at any point in his career and less time talking to data scientists than ever.

2. Tom “regrets that product management exists,” but this isn't an insult to PMs. Tom argues that PM is a trade, not a qualification—a muscle built by reps. Hiring too many PMs as a default takes reps away from engineers and designers, infantilizing people perfectly capable of good decisions who never had to make them because “there was always a PM to babysit them.”

3. AI is exposing rampant “product theater.” Stakeholder management, alignment, storytelling—real work, but not product work, and they’re what the industry has rewarded PMs for the past five years. But theater only survives where real work is expensive to verify, and it isn't anymore. Every Whatnot hire is given a problem and a dataset and defends a POV out loud — and you watch how quickly the thinking decays in people who can present but can't think clearly.

4. The PM skill trending up fastest: systems thinking. Tom asks this question in every product review: “What do we do if the experiment is green? What do we do if it’s red?” If the answer is “I don’t know,” you haven't done the mental work necessary to run this experiment.

5. Stop promoting your A-players out of the work they’re great at. The common trap: take an A-player PM, make them a director, tell them to stop being hands-on, watch their instincts atrophy while junior PMs yo-yo the same PRD through review. At Whatnot, the four or five PM managers each spend at least 90% of their time on IC work; Tom spends about half his time as CPO as an IC. 

6. “It’s really complex” is usually code for weak leadership. Twitter ran working groups on lifting the 140-character limit for Tom’s entire tenure. Everyone knew it was inevitable—Japanese users tweeted six times as often because kanji packs more meaning per character—but nobody would make the call. It shipped almost two years after he left, and nothing bad happened. When something seems complicated, ask whether it’s actually complicated or whether leadership just won’t decide.

7. Map PMs to problems, not teams. Every six months, Tom, the CEO, and senior leads define the company strategy and key pillars, then assign DRIs by skill set. Some engineering teams go a year without a PM. The result: a PM who’s worked on buyer, seller, and trust problems instead of spending three years on notifications. More reps, more muscle groups.

8. Averages mean nothing to the individual. This is the thread running through Tom’s worst decisions. A feature only 3% of users touch looks like a deprecation candidate—until you go a layer deeper and find that for some users it’s 100% of their use case, and killing it is like “a Westfield mall turning off the power in the lead-up to Christmas.” Always ask what distribution hides under the average, and when the anecdote conflicts with the data, trust the anecdote.

9. True PMF is something you feel before you see it in the data. Twitter had nine heads of product in the two years Tom was there and survived anyway, because the product had a level of PMF that absorbed extraordinary mismanagement. Elon changed the name, brand, team, and culture; the network effects held. The career lesson: work somewhere with true PMF early so you learn what bottled lightning actually feels like.

10. End turf wars by giving one person both sides of the tradeoff. At Twitch, discovery and ads were perpetually at war for impressions. One of Tom’s first moves was to put ads inside discovery under a single PM accountable for total GMV from the feed, organic and paid alike. The tradeoff gets made naturally, cutting months of back-and-forth and the politics that turn decisions from company-first to career-first.

title:
Why autonomous discovery is stalling on hardware, not algorithms

The algorithms are ready. The hardware is not. That is the argument of this review, and it reframes where the bottleneck in autonomous
content:
Why autonomous discovery is stalling on hardware, not algorithms

The algorithms are ready. The hardware is not. That is the argument of this review, and it reframes where the bottleneck in autonomous discovery actually sits.

Richard Canty and Milad Abolhasani trace self-driving labs from 1970s liquid handlers to today's closed-loop platforms. The numbers are not subtle. Artificial Chemist identified eleven distinct perovskite quantum dot formulations in 30 hours using under 210 ml of reagents. AlphaFlow navigated a 40-parameter reaction space with less than 0.2% of the reagents an equivalent manual search would need. Fast-Cat mapped a two-objective Pareto front for rhodium-catalysed hydroformylation in 60 experiments, replacing screens of over 400 runs.

So why is this not everywhere? Optimization was never the hard part. AI suites already propose experiments and estimate uncertainty faster than any rig generates data. Meanwhile most platforms are bespoke assemblies of pumps, valves and reactors tuned to one narrow envelope. Retooling from electrochemical screening to organometallic catalysis means downtime and safety revalidation.

The consequence for anyone training models on experimental data is sharp. Identical protocols give divergent results across labs because reactor geometry, optical alignment and sensor calibration never make it into the digital record. No amount of model capacity fixes an uncalibrated sensor. The authors argue the real barrier is missing process-complete metadata: provenance of raw materials, how precursors were made, the apparatus itself. Until hardware is described as rigorously as software is shared, reproducibility caps out below algorithmic potential.

Two points I keep returning to. First, co-design: putting device-level figures of merit directly in the objective, so the agent optimizes solar cell efficiency rather than synthetic yield, with multifidelity surrogates carrying uncertainty across the synthesis to performance hierarchy. Second, where agents belong. Planning and supervision, yes. Real-time actuation, interlocks and safety-critical control should stay deterministic and formally verifiable.

The near-term move is unglamorous and high return: instrument your existing platforms for full process capture before scaling autonomy. The compounding asset is not the robot, it is the dataset another lab can trust. Also worth noting, in a survey of 54 researchers, 74% did not want total automation, with hypothesis generation the function they most wanted to keep.

Paper: Canty & Abolhasani, Nature Reviews Chemistry (2026) — journal license | https://t.co/YxfSLXQtvV

title:

That is the phas
content:
⚡️California’s Democratic Party endorsement shows the ideological center of gravity has moved beyond taxing income toward challenging the legitimacy of extreme private wealth itself.

That is the phase shift.

The billionaire is no longer treated merely as a rich taxpayer.

The billionaire is increasingly treated as a rival center of power.

That changes the political objective.

Revenue becomes only part of the motive.

The deeper motive is subordination.

The state wants to establish that no private balance sheet sits beyond public claim, even when the wealth has not been sold, distributed, or converted into cash.

A wealth tax reaches into ownership itself.

That makes it qualitatively different from higher income or capital-gains taxes.

The state begins taxing the continued possession of accumulated power.

The coalition supporting this believes concentrated wealth already governs too much of society through capital allocation, media ownership, philanthropy, lobbying, technology, housing, and political access. Taxation becomes a tool for reducing that independent power, not merely funding programs.

That is why the argument will spread.

AI will increase the political pressure.

The next productivity wave will reward ownership of models, chips, platforms, data, energy, and equity far more than ordinary labor. A small number of people will accumulate fortunes at a speed the political system cannot culturally absorb.

The public will see machine-driven abundance alongside professional displacement, wage compression, housing scarcity, and concentrated ownership.

The demand to tax wealth will become stronger because the ownership gap will become harder to defend through traditional merit narratives.

The technology class helped finance the political culture now turning against it because it believed social liberalism and capital accumulation could remain permanently aligned.

That bargain is ending.

Progressive politics accepted concentrated wealth while that wealth funded its institutions, media, nonprofits, universities, and campaigns.

The emerging faction sees the concentration itself as the violation.

Moving to Texas solves state residency exposure.

It does not solve national political exposure.

It also does not solve reputational exposure, federal taxation, corporate regulation, antitrust pressure, or the growing belief that geographic exit is proof of disloyalty.

The claim that this automatically becomes federal policy in 2028 is overstated.

The constitutional, legislative, electoral, and enforcement barriers are real.

The more likely outcome is that wealth taxation becomes a required Democratic primary position before it becomes enacted federal law.

Candidates will endorse the principle.

The details will remain vague.

The policy will function first as a loyalty test.

That matters because political normalization precedes legislation.

Once every major candidate accepts that accumulated wealth is a legitimate annual tax base, the argument has already crossed the hardest cultural threshold.

The implementation can come later through narrower mechanisms:

higher estate taxes,

mark-to-market taxation,

minimum taxes on unrealized gains,

limits on borrowing against appreciated assets,

exit taxes,

trust restrictions,

and tighter treatment of foundations and private holdings.

A direct federal wealth tax may fail.

The state can still construct its economic equivalent through multiple channels.

The wealthy respond by reorganizing ownership, residency, trusts, liquidity, citizenship, and political giving.

The state responds by expanding reporting, coordination, valuation rules, and exit penalties.

Capital mobility then becomes evidence for stronger enforcement.

Stronger enforcement accelerates mobility.

The loop hardens.

The larger political consequence is a durable split between the Democratic Party and the entrepreneurial class that once financed much of its ascent.

・スムーズさの正体は「ターン検出器の廃止」。従来の音声AIは、話す・聞くを交互に切り替えるトランシーバー方式で、発話が終わった瞬間を小さな専用モデルが当てにいく作りだった。早すぎると途中で遮られ、遅すぎると
content:
先日話題になった GPT-Live、どう作られているかの技術情報が OpenAI から公開されました。なんであんなにやり取りがスムーズなのか、不思議に思っていた人も多いのではないでしょうか。

・スムーズさの正体は「ターン検出器の廃止」。従来の音声AIは、話す・聞くを交互に切り替えるトランシーバー方式で、発話が終わった瞬間を小さな専用モデルが当てにいく作りだった。早すぎると途中で遮られ、遅すぎると反応が鈍い。GPT-Live は話しながら同時に聞ける「電話」(全二重)にして、この発話終わり当てゲーム自体をなくした

・「しゃべる」と「考える」の分離。会話は音声モデルが回し続け、深い推論やツール実行は GPT-5.5 などに裏で非同期に投げる。だから考え込みの沈黙が起きない

・メディア処理は Python asyncio から Go に書き直し。「たまに遅い」の遅い側が、旧システムの平常運転と同じ速さになった

・接続も自作。WebRTC の6往復のハンドシェイクを1往復に畳むプロトコル WARP を作って IETF に提案中。セッション開始は UDP パケット1個から

これは自分の話ですが、実は GPT-Live リリース直後に、これを使って継続的に英語学習ができる簡単なアプリを作って OpenAI のアプリ申請を出したのですが、まったく承認されません。。なので、使いたい人が自分で入れられる形で出そうかなと思っています。

content:
Claude Codeは、僕の働き方を100%変えた。

今まで1日12時間以上デスクにいたのが、今は多くても2時間。

残りは全部、自然の中を散歩したり、考え事にふけっていたり、自分のクリエイティビティとかプロダクティビティを上げる活動に使っている。下の写真はワルシャワの川で、最近みんなとカヌーをしていた時のこと。もちろんこの間も、全ての仕事は動いています。

ただし、使い方を間違えたら意味がない。

Claude Codeを使い倒すためのコツを共有します。

1. 自分で作業させるんじゃなくて、任せるために使う。まず指揮者役のオーケストレーターを1つ立てて、自分はそこにだけ指示を出す。実際の作業は全部、オーケストレーターが別のエージェントに振り分ける。自分が触るのは1箇所だけ。あとは勝手に分配されて、並行で走っていく

2. 委任した作業の進捗を、こまめに確認させる。委任先のエージェントは、思っていたより高い確率で黙って失敗する。オーケストレーター側を「参謀長」として、委任先を常に見張らせることで、ちゃんと仕事が進んでいる状態を担保できる

3. 音声入力のツールは、まだ正解が見つかってない。僕は今AquaVoiceを使ってるけど、正直、精度があまり良くない。もう少しマシなものに乗り換える必要があると感じてる。ここは引き続き探してる

4. 外出中は、調べ物や作業の結果をHTMLサイトとして作らせるといい。そうすればパソコンに戻った時に、エージェントが終わらせた仕事が、きれいなHTMLで説明された状態で待っている

5. 今の一番のお気に入りルーティン。朝起きたら、まず水をたくさん飲む。そこで、その日やらなきゃいけないことを全部、頭からオーケストレーターにぶちまける。それから朝ごはんを作って、食べる。瞑想して、今日をどう過ごしたいかをジャーナルに書く。コーヒーを淹れる。ここまで終わってから、AIに任せられない仕事に取り掛かる。つまり、僕が朝の時間を自分のために使ってる間に、エージェントたちは全部動き終わってる。このルーティン、そのままパクってください

僕はたぶん、日本人でトップクラスにClaude Codeを実務へ突っ込んでる方だと思う。本気でこの技術に驚かされてる。

このコツを実践してClaude Codeを使い倒せば、生産性は100倍になる。約束します。

content:
UberのCTOが、めちゃくちゃ大事なこと言ってる。

多くの人は「AIエージェントのセキュリティ＝プロンプトインジェクション対策（AIを言葉で騙す攻撃を防ぐこと）」だと思ってるが、実際は全然違う。

Uberは1日5万件以上のAIエージェントの動きを本番で10ヶ月監視して、こういう優先順位が見えてきた👇

1. 侵入手口（プロンプトインジェクション）への対策
2. 認証情報（パスワードやAPIキー）の漏えい対策 ← 実際はここが圧倒的多数
3. 承認フローが形だけになっていないかの対策
4. 個別のツール呼び出しの監視

大事なのは2番目と3番目。

実際に多かったのは派手な攻撃ではなく、「機密情報がうっかり漏れる」という地味な事故だった（26カテゴリ、数百件を検知）。

そして1セッションで50件以上の承認を求められると、人間はもう読まずに押すだけになる。「人がチェックしてるから安全」という前提そのものが崩れる。

だからセキュリティの単位は「1回のツール操作」ではなく「一連のワークフロー全体」でマルっと見る必要がある。

攻撃は、単体では無害に見える操作の積み重ねの中に隠れているから。

要するに、AIエージェントを守るために本当に効くのは、派手な攻撃検知よりも地味な情報漏えい対策と「ちゃんと見る」承認フローの設計、ということ。

Uberはこの検知システムと評価用ベンチマークを今日オープンソース化。気になる人は是非チェックを。

title: It has long been an open secret that the United States is "weaponizing" AI technology. Whether for military applications, espionage, or cyberattacks, the U.S. is undoubtedly reinforcing this role and
content:
It has long been an open secret that the United States is "weaponizing" AI technology. Whether for military applications, espionage, or cyberattacks, the U.S. is undoubtedly reinforcing this role and status, with China clearly serving as the primary target.

In response, China has begun to implement a systematic defense strategy—a comprehensive "combo" of measures balancing development and security. These include establishing a sovereign technology ecosystem, advancing tiered and classified regulation, mandating the labeling of AI-generated content, and advocating for Global South-led multilateral governance. These steps aim to comprehensively prevent and mitigate potential risks arising from U.S. AI technology monopolies, as well as associated threats such as hacking, political infiltration, and supply chain cutoffs.

1.  **Strengthening domestic "technological sovereignty" to overcome supply chain cutoffs and technological dependency.** In response to frequent U.S. chip export controls and potential sanctions against Chinese AI laboratories, China is prioritizing indigenous R&D as its fundamental defense: **Accelerating the substitution of domestic computing power and chips:** Going all-out to catch up and build an independent ecosystem comprising domestically produced advanced-process AI chips, large-scale models, and foundational software. **Developing high-performance open-source ecosystems:** Launching cost-effective large language models (such as the recent Kimi K3) and releasing their weights globally to break the market monopoly and technological blockade imposed by proprietary, closed U.S. models. **Curating high-quality industrial-grade datasets:** Leveraging the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC) to release high-value AI application scenarios and high-quality industry datasets for central state-owned enterprises, thereby establishing data barriers in key real-economy sectors that are difficult for U.S. technology to penetrate.

2.  **Refining full-lifecycle legislation to guard against cyberattacks and data security risks.** China is deeply concerned about the potential dangers posed by U.S. AI models in cyberspace, including novel security threats such as autonomous model intrusion, data poisoning, and adversarial attacks. **Incorporating AI risks into the *Cybersecurity Law*:** The newly revised and implemented *Cybersecurity Law* explicitly includes provisions for AI risk monitoring, assessment, and security regulation. **Advancing comprehensive *Artificial Intelligence Law* legislation:** The State Council has fast-tracked this legislation, aiming to establish a fundamental framework for tiered and classified AI regulation and define liability boundaries. **Conducting routine cyber offense-defense drills:** In critical information infrastructure sectors—such as digital government, finance, and energy—authorities are conducting regular simulations of extreme scenarios like "model poisoning" and "deepfakes," while establishing unified mechanisms for emergency response and service suspension or interruption.

 🔍 3. Implementing precise control over content and services to safeguard regime security and social stability. The Chinese government strictly prevents external models from bypassing national censorship mechanisms and has issued a series of targeted regulations addressing issues such as AI-generated misinformation, algorithmic bias, and psychological dependency: Labeling system for AI-generated and synthetic content: The *Measures for the Labeling of AI-Generated and Synthetic Content* will take effect in September 2025, mandating that all interactive AI systems and generated content carry both visible and invisible labels to curb politically and economically motivated deepfake fraud originating from abroad. Targeted regulation for specific scenarios: For instance, the *Interim Measures for the Administration of AI-Based Anthropomorphic Interactive Services* (effective July 2026) apply a "prudent yet inclusive" and tiered classification approach to AI products that simulate human thought and emotional interaction, aiming to prevent risks such as the distortion of values ​​and emotional manipulation among youth and the general public.

🌐 4. Promoting multilateral governance and resisting "AI Monroeism." On the international stage, China firmly opposes the US use of its AI technological advantages to engage in "technological smearing" and "AI hegemony": Issuance of the *Action Plan for Global AI Governance*: China advocates for six key principles—including AI for good and the benefit of the people, respect for sovereignty, a development-oriented approach, and ensuring security and controllability—while insisting on the United Nations as the primary channel for the collaborative formulation of rules. Uniting the Global South: Twenty-nine nations jointly signed the agreement to establish the "World AI Cooperation Organization" (headquartered in Shanghai); through South-South cooperation, the initiative seeks to enhance the technological sovereignty of developing nations and collectively counter the exclusive AI geopolitical rules dominated by Western countries.

title:
🧭 Long-Horizon Agents Need More Than Bigger Context Windows
AI Agents are moving from short conversations into software engineering, deep research, computer use and scientific discovery.
The new quest
content:
🧭 Long-Horizon Agents Need More Than Bigger Context Windows
AI Agents are moving from short conversations into software engineering, deep research, computer use and scientific discovery.
The new question is no longer whether a model can make one intelligent decision. It is whether an Agent can survive hundreds or thousands of dependent actions without forgetting its goal, corrupting its context or turning one small mistake into a failed trajectory.
Zhihu contributor 卡卡卡卡比 summarizes a new 149-page survey from the Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence at Renmin University of China.
Covering nearly 1,000 studies, systems and engineering practices, the survey proposes a unified view:
Long-horizon intelligence is a property of the entire Model-Harness system, not the model alone.

1️⃣ Running longer is not the same as long-horizon intelligence
METR measurements suggest that the human-equivalent task duration frontier Agents can complete at a 50% success rate has grown from seconds to more than ten hours.
The estimated doubling time is around 6.5 months across the full period, or 4.3 months when fitted from 2023 onward.
Estimates beyond roughly 16 hours remain uncertain because current task sets have limited coverage.
More importantly, elapsed time alone is a poor definition. A process can run for hours while making only loosely connected decisions.
A true long-horizon task contains many logical dependencies. Earlier decisions change later states, and local errors can propagate through the entire trajectory.

2️⃣ Why long trajectories fail
The survey groups common failures into three categories:
🔹 Goal drift and error accumulation
After thousands of steps, an Agent may gradually move away from the original objective. Small local mistakes are repeatedly inherited until the complete plan breaks.
🔹 Context corruption and window pressure
More context is not always better. Old plans, irrelevant logs and tool outputs can overwhelm useful state. Agents may also terminate prematurely when they sense that the context window is running out.
🔹 Sparse rewards and irreversible actions
Many tasks provide feedback only at the end, making credit assignment difficult. Meanwhile, deleting data, granting permissions or modifying production systems may create damage that cannot be easily reversed.
Larger models and longer context windows help, but they do not solve these system-level failures by themselves.

3️⃣ The core framework: Harness × Model
The model provides reasoning and action policies. The Harness manages everything required to keep those policies useful over time.
It decides when the model runs, what information it sees, which tools it can access, how actions are executed and verified, and what state survives across steps.
The same foundation model may therefore show very different capability, cost and reliability inside different Harnesses.
The survey describes a continuous feedback loop:
The Harness externalizes planning, memory, tools, verification and recovery.
Real interactions generate trajectories, failures and feedback.
Fine-tuning, reinforcement learning and distillation absorb these capabilities into the model.
The stronger model can then operate a more sophisticated Harness.
Long-horizon capability emerges from this co-evolution.

4️⃣ Three levels of long-horizon capability
The survey defines three nested levels instead of measuring tasks only by runtime.
🔹 H1 / C1: Within-window interactive reasoning
The task fits inside one context window, but requires repeated planning, action, observation and correction.
🔹 H2 / C2: Cross-session state and memory
The task lasts hours or days. The Agent must externalize state, create checkpoints, compress history and resume accurately after interruption.
🔹 H3 / C3: Learning across task streams
The Agent faces an open stream of changing tasks. It must accumulate reusable skills, generalize from experience and continue improving as tools, goals and environments change.
C2 depends on reliable C1 behavior. C3 requires both. An Agent cannot learn across tasks if it cannot reason consistently within one task or preserve state across sessions.

5️⃣ The control plane moved from prompts to runtimes
The survey describes three stages in Agent system development:
🔹 Prompt Engineering, 2020–2023
Control focused on instructions, chain-of-thought prompting, decomposition and self-correction within a single model call.
🔹 Context Engineering, 2023–2025
Systems began actively selecting retrieval results, tool outputs, conversation history and compressed summaries. The central question became: what should the model see at each step?
🔹 Runtime Harness, 2025–present
Control now extends to tools, memory, workflows, permissions, verification, recovery and multi-Agent coordination.
A production Harness therefore needs six connected components: workflows, context and memory, tools and skills, orchestration, hooks and middleware, and external verification.
The Harness is not merely a wrapper. It is the state machine, controller and safety boundary for the complete Agent.

6️⃣ Internal optimization must learn from entire trajectories
Harness engineering helps an Agent complete tasks at runtime. Model optimization makes the underlying policy better suited to long trajectories.
The survey maps a full training pipeline covering:
Long-context and state-efficient architectures
Task, environment and trajectory synthesis
Pre-training and mid-training
Curriculum-based fine-tuning
Agent reinforcement learning
On-policy distillation
Online self-evolution
Training data must contain more than final answers. It needs environment feedback, intermediate state, tool results, failed attempts and recovery trajectories.
Optimization must also move beyond single-step accuracy. The real objective is whether the complete trajectory remains efficient, recoverable and consistent with its final constraints.

7️⃣ Four frontiers define the next stage
The survey organizes future research around four axes:
🔹 Evolution
Harnesses must become reusable and self-improving, while useful experience is gradually converted into persistent model capabilities.
🔹 Effectiveness
Agents need realistic, verifiable environments. The next bottleneck may be environment construction and sample-efficient interaction rather than model size alone.
🔹 Efficiency
Agents must learn to allocate token, time and financial budgets dynamically. They need to know when to reason deeply, compress context, switch models or stop.
🔹 Trustworthiness
Long trajectories amplify mistakes and permission risks. Reliable autonomy requires sandboxes, approval gates, least-privilege access, provenance tracking, external verification and recovery mechanisms.
The survey makes one particularly important point: production permissions and safety boundaries primarily live in the Harness, not in model weights.
Model alignment is necessary, but it cannot decide which tools may run, which actions require approval or which experiences should be remembered.

🔑 The real meaning of “long horizon”
The next Agent breakthrough is not simply about remaining active for more hours.
It is about preserving goals, state and safety across increasingly long chains of dependent decisions.
A capable long-horizon Agent must always know what it is trying to accomplish, what has already happened, what went wrong and when it should stop.
That requires models and runtime systems to evolve together.

It also says the Max weights and Qwen3.8-27B will be released next week.
Zhihu contributor AI解码师 sees this as a strategic shift: Alibaba is choosing open ecosystem influence over keeping its strongest model exclusive to paid APIs.

1️⃣ Why open the Max model now?
Alibaba’s previous Max models remained closed, while its open-weight lineup stopped around Qwen3-235B.
The author argues that DeepSeek and other open models have weakened the premium of closed systems. Opening Qwen3.8-Max allows Alibaba to compete for developers, infrastructure support and downstream adoption at the 2.4T scale.

2️⃣ Extreme sparsity keeps inference manageable
Only 95B of Qwen3.8-Max’s 2.4T parameters are activated per token, an activation rate of roughly 4%.
Qwen3-235B-A22B activates close to 10%. Qwen3.8-Max therefore uses much higher sparsity to access a larger parameter pool without paying dense-model inference costs.
The author expects offloading to make experimentation possible for more teams. Actual deployment requirements will remain unclear until the weights, quantized versions and serving tools are released.

3️⃣ Its main strength is long-horizon work
Qwen3.8-Max performs strongly on tasks requiring long contexts and repeated tool use:
🔹 PaperBench: 93.0, ahead of Fable 5 at 88.8
🔹 CoWorkBench: 74.8, close to 75.9
🔹 WideSearch: 81.9, roughly level with 81.2
These benchmarks test paper reproduction, professional work and deep search. The model must preserve one objective across many interactions instead of solving an isolated question.
The API also offers low, medium and xhigh reasoning-effort modes. Support for both OpenAI and Anthropic protocols makes it easier to test inside existing coding-Agent workflows.

4️⃣ Real projects show both progress and limits
The author tested Qwen3.8-Max on two coding tasks.
It migrated a Vue 2 component to Vue 3 with performance close to Claude.
On a harder task involving OpenTelemetry instrumentation across a Python service, it missed several edge-case spans. Cross-file reasoning and exhaustive coverage still lag behind the strongest closed models.

5️⃣ The pricing is aggressive
International API pricing is listed at:
· $2 per million input tokens
· $6 per million output tokens
· $0.25 per million cached tokens
According to the author, this is around one-quarter to one-sixth of leading Claude or GPT prices.
Cached input is particularly useful for Agents, which repeatedly reuse long prompts, codebases and tool histories.

🔑 Alibaba’s two-front strategy
Qwen3.8-Max targets closed models with a low-cost API while using open weights to attract researchers, infrastructure providers and private-deployment users.
As frontier models become more accessible, competition will increasingly move toward training data, Agent Harnesses, verification and production infrastructure.

content:
DAILY SITUATION RECAP:

OpenAI makes huge math progress. Over the weekend, the company announced that an internal version of their next major model (GPT-6?) discovered 10 major new results in math and computer science for just $2,000 in tokens1. This comes just a few weeks after an OpenAI model disproved the Erdős unit distance conjecture, the first major novel AI-driven result in mathematics. There is so, so much more to come.

Alibaba releases Qwen3.8. It’s still not quite as generally intelligent as Fable, but it beats it (and Sol) on a number of benchmarks: PaperBench, PerceptionBench, and OSWorld-Verified, for example. It can do serious long-horizon autonomous coding tasks and assist with AI research. It ranks the highest of any non-Anthropic model on TextArena, and has reached the Pareto frontier for front-end code. And it’s $2/$6 per million input/output tokens, cheaper than Kimi K3 ($3/$15) and much cheaper than Fable ($10/$50).

The White House has completed its AI framework. In June, President Trump issued an executive order directing federal agencies to create a classified cyber benchmark for frontier models and a voluntary framework for frontier labs to share their models with the government before public release. Tomorrow, OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Meta staff will meet with admin officials to discuss the completed framework.

CXMT is planning a new memory fab in Beijing. It currently operates one in Beijing and two in Hefei, the city where it’s headquartered. The company, the world’s fourth-largest memory manufacturer, is currently seeking to rapidly expand production to meet the insatiable demand for memory.

Zeiss says it can handle increased AI demand. The German company manufactures optical systems, including extremely precise mirrors used in ASML’s lithography machines.

China tightens circuit design protections. Under new rules set to go into effect in October, chip layout designs will be subject to stricter registration standards with penalties for infringement. China is also considering export controls on strategically important technologies.

The UK is open to AI regulation. Kanishka Narayan, the UK’s first Cabinet-level Minister of Artificial Intelligence, says that if Britain’s current voluntary pre-deployment testing regime isn’t enough to ensure safety, they may implement regulation. The UK AI Security Institute (AISI) makes Britain the only country other than America with pre-deployment access to frontier models.

TikTok is finalizing three settlements over addiction. The plaintiffs allege that the platform caused them to suffer from a combination of addiction, depression, anxiety, eating disorders, self-harm, and other mental health conditions. Two of the three are minors.

Base Power raises $1B at a $13B valuation led by Ribbit, Addition, Valor, and JPMorgan. @basepowerco builds home battery systems that both provide power to customers and can feed back into the grid during peak demand times.

Valar Atomics raises $1B at a $6B valuation led by Sequoia. @valaratomics builds mass-producible small modular reactors (SMRs) for use in factory production, data centers, and other industrial applications. Valar, founded in 2023, became the first private reactor to reach criticality outside of a national laboratory.

Amazon crosses $3T in market cap thanks to strong earnings, bolstered by cloud (AWS) and AI.

Written by @theojaffee. Read more at our link in bio.

content:
you can build your own small language model from scratch on your computer - this free app walks you through every step 🤯

it's called Language Model Builder, and it comes in two parts.

the first is a 90-minute interactive textbook. 

it covers the fundamentals, tokenization, embeddings, attention, the transformer, training data, loss and gradient descent, fine-tuning. no coding or math background needed.

and instead of staring at diagrams, you run each experiment yourself as you read.

the second is a training workbench that runs the full pipeline locally on Apple's MLX:

> pre-train a base model on a dataset you pick
> fine-tune it with SFT, then align it with DPO
> watch the loss curve drop in real time as it learns
> chat with the model you made, with a token-probability x-ray view so you can see how it "thinks"

on default settings you'll get coherent, multi-paragraph text in about a day. 

a GPT-2-small-class model takes roughly a week on a high-end Mac. 

100% free, no account, runs entirely offline.

content:
AIが普及すれば、弁護士のアワリーチャージ自体がなくなる方向に向かう、というのは単純化しすぎていると思う。

そもそもアワリーチャージは「1時間働いたから1時間分請求する」というだけの仕組みではない。
依頼を受けた時点では、どこに論点が潜んでいるか、相手方からのあり得る反論はどんなものか、調査や交渉にどれだけ時間がかかるか、誰にも正確には分からない。つまり、仕事が始まる前に「この案件はいくらです」と約束すること自体が難しい。だから「かかった時間」で精算することで、その不確実性を依頼者と分け合ってきたという背景があるはず。
AIで10時間の仕事が1時間になったとしても、この不確実性がなくなるわけではない。だからアワリーチャージがすぐになくなるとは思わない。

本当に変化が起きるのは、依頼者側もAIを使って「この業務に本当に10時間必要なのか」「ジュニアの作業にこの単価を払う必要があるのか」「他の事務所ならいくらでできるのか」を検証できるようになったときだと思う。

つまりAIが壊すのは時間課金そのものではなく、時間、専門性、品質の関係を依頼者が確認できなかったという、アワリーチャージを支えてきた情報の非対称性だと思う。

そして、その先でも、高度な交渉、訴訟戦略、危機対応のように希少な判断力や信用が価値になる領域では、時間単価はむしろ上がっていくはず。AI時代に起きるのはアワリーチャージの消滅ではなく、「作業量に対する課金」と「希少な判断力に対する課金」の分離というあたりかなと。

content:
GEMA v. Suno判決。現時点では判決文が公開されてないのでミュンヘン第一地方裁判所のリリースと報道から推測する限りとして、基本的な判断枠組みは以前に自分が記事を書いたGEMA v. OpenAI判決と枠組みは変わらないように見える。すなわち、モデルへの記憶理論である。

特定の著作物と類似した出力をAIモデルから生成できることを根拠として、モデル内部に著作物が「記憶」されていると評価し、その記憶自体を著作権法上の複製と捉える。さらに、類似した生成物の出力も別個の侵害とし、ユーザーがプロンプトを入力した場合であっても、学習データを選択し、モデルを設計・運営しているAI事業者を直接の責任主体とする構造である。OpenAI事件で歌詞について示された法理を、Suno事件ではメロディー、ハーモニー、リズム等の楽曲そのものへ適用したものと整理できるのだろう。

一方、今回の判決にはOpenAI事件になかった重要な上乗せがある。Sunoの学習が米国で行われたにも関わらず、ドイツの裁判所がその学習行為について米国著作権法を適用し、フェアユースの成立まで否定したとされる点である。ドイツ法上のモデル内複製や事業者責任の判断自体は従来路線の延長であるが、外国で行われた学習行為にまで踏み込み、米国のフェアユースを否定した点では、GEMA v. OpenAIよりも国際的な射程が広く、かなり攻めた判決だと思う。有効性はさておき。

もっとも、出力の類似性だけからモデル内部に著作権法上の「複製物」が存在すると認定できるのか、またドイツの裁判所による米国フェアユースの評価が上級審でも維持されるのかは今後の大きな争点となる。

ということで、判決文を待っている者は多そうという話もあるが、何と言うかGEMA v. OpenAIでのAIモデルへの記憶理論が音楽でも使われたわけで欧州では定着していくかもしれないなぁと思うところも。

title: Afghanistan humanitarian crisis has intensified since Taliban’s return to power, rights group reports
content: Human Rights Watch (HRW) on Monday reported that in the five years since the Taliban’s resurgence , the group has fostered a hostile environment and spurred one of the world’s worst human rights crises. HRW called on governments around the world to take decisive action as opposed to passively providing condolences, stating that the international response should match the scale of the crisis. HRW called upon countries around the world to support these international bodies in their work so that women, children, and other Afghan citizens may see relief from perpetual human rights abuses. Fereshta Abbasi, an Afghanistan researcher at HRW, stated: “The fifth anniversary of the Taliban takeover is a grim marker of the devastating costs of impunity. Governments should move beyond statements of concern and press for justice for serious crimes in Afghanistan, including the crime against humanity of gender persecution.” Since the Taliban returned to power in August of 2021, the country’s turbulent social and political climate has been comprised of a reported decline of rights for women and girls, a lack of food security, restrictions on press freedoms , mass displacement, and hostilities with Pakistan . Now the country, which has continually ranked last in Georgetown’s Women, Peace, and Security Index, faces a catastrophe that may only be cured by overwhelming international support. The Islamic fundamentalist group has adapted social prohibitions for women into an intense legal and administrative framework , promulgating laws denying women access to anything more than an elementary education, restricting access to healthcare , dissolving the minimum age for legal marriage, and removing domestic violence protections . UN Women has indicated that more than 10 million women are in need of humanitarian aid in Afghanistan. Additionally, nearly one-third of the population is facing acute food insecurity spurred by blocked supply routes, crop fail
author: Abigail Austin | Vermont Law & Graduate School, US

title: Russia-linked airstrike in Mali may violate international law, rights group warns
content: Human Rights Watch (HRW) on Friday condemned a deadly airstrike by the Russia’s-Africa Corps in central Mali, saying the strike appeared to be an arbitrary attack that may have violated international humanitarian law. The Russian government-controlled Africa Corps launched the airstrike that killed eight civilians, including three children, on June 15. The strike hit the Kyrnia village in Mali’s Mopti region, an area controlled for about six years by al-Qaeda-linked armed group Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM). Although Africa Corps later claimed it had targeted a gathering of terrorist fighters, HRW said it found no evidence that JNIM fighters were among those killed. The rights group based its findings on interviews with eye-witnesses, Malian military sources, local journalists, and community leaders, as well as satellite imagery, photographs, and a video released by Africa Corps. The organization said its analysis of the footage confirmed the strike took place in Kyrnia and identified Africa Corps as responsible for the attack. HRW also sent its findings to Russia’s defence minister on July 22 but said it received no response. Under international humanitarian law , parties to an armed conflict must distinguish between civilians and combatants, direct attacks only at specific military objectives, ensure expected civilian harm is not excessive in relation to the anticipated military advantage, and take all feasible precautions to minimize civilian casualties. HRW said the available evidence indicates these obligations were not met. On June 23, Africa Corps announced it had carried out a successful strike against what it described as a “gathering place of terrorist groups” in the Mopti region, claiming several JNIM commanders had been killed. HRW disputed that account and claimed they could not find evidence that any militants were among the fatalities. The village chief, who was killed in the strike, was reportedly a wealthy trader whos
author: Tiana Nowzari | Lincoln Alexander School of Law, CA

title: Pakistan dispatch: deadly clashes in Azad Jammu and Kashmir escalate political crisis
content: Pakistan-administered territories of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) are witnessing one of their most serious episodes of political unrest in recent years, as protests led by Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) have escalated into deadly confrontations with security forces, disrupting elections, transport, and public life across several districts. While AJK enjoys some level of autonomy, it does not possess full state sovereignty because ultimate decision-making authority rests with Pakistan. As a result, local institutions are held accountable for public dissatisfaction despite lacking the authority to address its underlying causes. According to Pakistani and International media reports, the latest wave of unrest began on July 27 in Rawalkot, Muzaffarabad, Mirpur, Kotli and neighboring areas, where demonstrations over governance, electoral reforms, and constitutional issues have intensified. Clashes between protesters and law enforcement agencies have resulted in multiple fatalities and injuries, although official figures differ from those reported by protest organizers and independent rights groups. Pakistan media reported that security forces and police confronted protesters attempting to march towards major administrative centers. Azad Jammu and Kashmir police alleged that some demonstrators used automatic weapons during confrontations, resulting in the death of at least one Rangers official and injuries to several police personnel. Authorities have maintained that security forces acted to restore public order after the protest turned violent. The JAAC has disputed the government’s official narrative, accusing authorities of using excessive force against peaceful demonstrators. Protest leaders claim significantly higher civilian casualties than those acknowledged by public officials, accusing the government of suppressing dissent through arrests and placing restrictions on movement. author: Syeda Aamna Hasan | Brunel University, GB

title: Amnesty International calls global extreme heat a human rights emergency
content: Marta Schaaf, Amnesty International’s program director for climate, social justice and corporate accountability, said Wednesday in a statement that the extreme heat driving wildfires, drought and floods across multiple continents amounts to a human rights emergency. She urged national governments to protect people now and to confront the fossil fuel industry Amnesty blames for the crisis. Schaaf tied the crisis to corporate greed and government failure. “This heat is political… It is a human rights emergency that threatens the rights to life, health, housing, water and sanitation, food, education, and a healthy environment.” She added that “[t]hese harms are being made worse by authoritarian tactics that attack climate science, restrict protest, spread climate disinformation and shield powerful fossil fuel interests from accountability.” She described extreme heat as “a multiplier of human rights harm,” rather than a stand-alone disaster. Amnesty’s statement lands amid mounting evidence of the toll that extreme heat has taken globally. The World Health Organization’s heat-and-health fact sheet says the number of people exposed to extreme heat is climbing steeply in every region this century. It estimates roughly 489,000 heat-related deaths annually between 2000 and 2019. It also finds that heat mortality among people over 65 rose about 85 percent over two decades. Those figures go in tandem with a summer of heat records in 2026. Successive heat domes have put tens of millions of Americans under heat alerts , and federal data show the contiguous United States recorded its second-hottest first half of any year in 2026. In Europe, French authorities attributed several thousand excess deaths to a June heatwave. title: Attorney says Trump administration defied court order by moving transgender inmates to segregated unit
content: An attorney for several incarcerated transgender women argued Wednesday that the Trump administration violated a court order by transferring them to a segregated prison unit, and urged a federal judge to enforce the order. Judge Royce C. Lamberth of the US District Court for the District of Columbia heard the argument in Doe v. McHenry , No. 1:25-cv-00286 (since consolidated with two related suits and captioned Jane Doe v. Blanche ) on the plaintiffs’ motion to return them to the general population of women’s prisons and to bar any further transfers into the segregated unit. The dispute stems from a June 7 preliminary injunction in which Lamberth directed prison officials to house the plaintiffs in women’s prisons or women’s halfway houses. He also enjoined enforcement of part of Executive Order 14168 (“the EO”), which President Donald Trump signed on Jan. 20, 2025. Section 4(a) of that order (“the Transfer Provision”) instructs the Attorney General and the Secretary of Homeland Security to ensure that males are not housed in women’s facilities; Section 4(c) directs the discontinuation of gender-affirming medical care. Under Sections 2(b) and 2(e) of the EO, “male” means “a person belonging, at conception, to the sex that produces the small reproductive cell,” while “women” and “girls” mean “adult and juvenile human females,” respectively. Lamberth did not rule from the bench on the plaintiffs’ request. He did appear to agree with the plaintiffs’ attorney, however, saying that the transfers appear to violate his order “on its face” by isolating the plaintiffs and stripping them of the privileges they had held in women’s facilities.
